From 1635c2acdde86c4f555b627aec873c8677c421ed Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: NeilBrown <neilb@ownmail.net>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 09:18:21 +1100
Subject: [PATCH] cachefiles: fix incorrect dentry refcount in
 cachefiles_cull()

The patch mentioned below changed cachefiles_bury_object() to expect 2
references to the 'rep' dentry.  Three of the callers were changed to
use start_removing_dentry() which takes an extra reference so in those
cases the call gets the expected references.

However there is another call to cachefiles_bury_object() in
cachefiles_cull() which did not need to be changed to use
start_removing_dentry() and so was not properly considered.
It still passed the dentry with just one reference so the net result is
that a reference is lost.

To meet the expectations of cachefiles_bury_object(), cachefiles_cull()
must take an extra reference before the call.  It will be dropped by
cachefiles_bury_object().

Reported-by: Marc Dionne <marc.dionne@auristor.com>
Fixes: 7bb1eb45e43c ("VFS: introduce start_removing_dentry()")
Signed-off-by: NeilBrown <neil@brown.name>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/177456350181.1851489.16359967086642190170@noble.neil.brown.name
Acked-by: Paulo Alcantara (Red Hat) <pc@manguebit.org>
Signed-off-by: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/cachefiles/namei.c b/fs/cachefiles/namei.c
index e5ec90dccc27..eb9eb7683e3c 100644
--- a/fs/cachefiles/namei.c
+++ b/fs/cachefiles/namei.c
@@ -810,6 +810,11 @@ int cachefiles_cull(struct cachefiles_cache *cache, struct dentry *dir,
 	if (ret < 0)
 		goto error_unlock;
 
+	/*
+	 * cachefiles_bury_object() expects 2 references to 'victim',
+	 * and drops one.
+	 */
+	dget(victim);
 	ret = cachefiles_bury_object(cache, NULL, dir, victim,
 				     FSCACHE_OBJECT_WAS_CULLED);
 	dput(victim);
-- 
2.34.1

### Modifications in each file

- **fs/cachefiles/namei.c**: Added a `dget(victim)` call before calling `cachefiles_bury_object()` in the `cachefiles_cull()` function. This ensures the victim dentry has two references when passed to `cachefiles_bury_object()`, as expected by that function (which drops one reference). Previously, only one reference (from an earlier lookup) was held, leading to a dentry refcount leak.

### Relationship between modifications

The change is isolated to a single file. The added `dget()` compensates for the reference-count expectation of `cachefiles_bury_object()`. Without this extra reference, the function would drop a reference not originally held, resulting in an incorrect dentry refcount. This fix restores correct balance in reference counting for the victim dentry in the culling path.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<ret = cachefiles_bury_object(cache, NULL, dir, victim,
                                     FSCACHE_OBJECT_WAS_CULLED);>
<dput(victim);>
Reason:
cachefiles_bury_object() expects two references to the victim dentry (it will drop one internally). Cachefiles_cull() only had one reference from cachefiles_lookup_for_cull(), and after the call, dput(victim) drops it again, leading to a net loss of one reference and a dentry refcount imbalance.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<+	dget(victim);
 	ret = cachefiles_bury_object(cache, NULL, dir, victim,
 				     FSCACHE_OBJECT_WAS_CULLED);>
<dput(victim); (unchanged)>
Reason:
Adding dget(victim) before the call provides the second reference that cachefiles_bury_object() expects. The function will then drop one reference internally, and the subsequent dput(victim) drops the other, restoring the correct reference count.
